nodes.title: Caption
widgets_values: Golden-hour light slants through a bamboo grove onto a giant panda sitting on mossy ground, a wide cinematic view with the bear placed left of centre. It grips a green stalk in both front paws and chews, its black-and-white fur glowing at the edges where the low sun catches it. Tall bamboo stems stretch away to the right, their leaves lit amber, and soft haze fills the gaps between them.

nodes.title: Read me
widgets_values:
# P-JiT: Linum's samples, seed for seed

**P-JiT 21K** by Linum: a 2B-parameter text-to-image model that works directly on pixels. Research checkpoint, with rough edges. Nodes: **ComfyUI-PJiT**.

**Files**:
- models/diffusion_models: [pjit_21k_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/PedroMarinhoDev/P-JiT-21K-ComfyUI/blob/main/diffusion_models/pjit_21k_bf16.safetensors), 4.4 GB: the same pictures as Linum's fp32 release. [pjit_21k_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/PedroMarinhoDev/P-JiT-21K-ComfyUI/blob/main/diffusion_models/pjit_21k_int8_convrot.safetensors), 2.3 GB, is about 1.8x faster with small changes in fine detail.
- models/text_encoders: [qwen3.5_4b_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Qwen3.5/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3.5_4b_bf16.safetensors) from Comfy-Org/Qwen3.5
- No VAE file: P-JiT has no latent space. Load VAE is set to the built-in **pixel_space**.

**Settings** (Linum's): **50 steps, euler, simple, cfg 15**, an empty negative prompt. Load P-JiT Model brings the guidance (APG) and the noise scale with it, so other samplers and step counts work, but these are what it was tuned on. The five sizes in P-JiT Empty Image are the ones it was trained at.

**Prompts**: it was trained on dense captions of 50 to 80 words saying what is visible, where, and how it is lit. Short prompts give noticeably worse images. It cannot draw text, signs or posters, and it struggles with full-body shots, crowds and interactions between several people.

This graph reproduces the published samples on any NVIDIA GPU. **P-JiT Noise (H100)** draws the noise exactly as an H100 draws it, and **P-JiT Scheduler** is the reference's exact schedule. The caption here is Linum's panda, seed 1, at 16:9. The others are in [their README](https://github.com/Linum-AI/pjit-21k#reproducing-the-samples). Expect the same picture with small differences in fine detail, about 40-48 dB: GPU rounding changes with the card and the attention kernel, and even their own code differs from itself by about that much when rerun in a different batch shape.
